en: The Sūtra on the Measurement of Merit and the Elimination of Obstacles and Eradication of Sins through the Divine Mantra of the Names of the Twelve Buddhas, Spoken by the Buddha;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of India during the Sui Dynasty.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Bhagavān was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain near the city of Rājagṛha.
He was accompanied by a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
as well as a great multitude of bodhisattvas numbering twelve thousand,
headed by the Bodhisattva Ajita.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Maitreya Bodhisattva, saying:
"Maitreya, to the east of this buddha-field, there are ten unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields, equal to the atoms in hundreds of thousands of millions of such fields."
Beyond the buddha-fields, there is a buddha-field named Liberation-Lord World (*Vimuktinātha*).
Within that world, there is a buddha.

He is named Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, King of Unobstructed Birth in the Dharma Realm, Adorned by the Transformations of the Power of Vows and the Radiance of Boundless Suns and Moons, Crown-Tuft Adorned with Various Ornaments, Fragrance of the Body of Vaidūrya Jewels, Lotus-Flower Radiance of the Features of Upright Virtue Equal to the Pure Atoms of the Void. Having completed his offerings of the most supreme fragrances, he is the one whose eyes are upright and whose marks are radiant with virtue.
Now, following the inclinations of his mind, he wanders at ease, preaching the Dharma wherever he is.
If there are good men or good women who have committed the four grave offenses or the five heinous crimes, or who have slandered the Triple Gem—
Furthermore, regarding one who commits the four *pārājika* offenses,
their sin is so heavy that even if the land of Jambudvīpa were reduced to atoms,
and each atom were to constitute one *kalpa*, [the duration of their suffering would still not be exhausted].
If such a person has committed offenses spanning many kalpas,
by reciting the name of even one Buddha and performing a single prostration,
all shall be completely extinguished and eliminated.
How much more so for one who receives, maintains, recites, and remembers it day and night without forgetting;
the merit of such a person is inconceivable. Furthermore, in that Buddha-world, there is a bodhisattva named Anupama.
The Tathāgata Unobstructed King bestowed upon that bodhisattva the prediction of his future attainment of buddhahood:

"He shall become a Buddha named Vairocana Unobstructed Eye Sovereign of All Marks Who Radiates Light Illumining All Buddha-fields in the Ten Directions, Whose Body is as Firm as Vajra, a Precious Lotus Flower of Splendid Marks and Sun-Moon Radiance, an Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One."
Furthermore, in that eastern direction,
there is another Buddha named Sarvavyūhavimalaprabha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
You should likewise invoke that Buddha’s name and cultivate reverence toward him.
One must also recite his name and keep that Buddha’s name in mind.
In the southern direction, there is a Buddha.
His name is Prajñāpāramitā-mālā; one should contemplate that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, and likewise recite that Buddha’s name and cultivate respectful devotion toward him.
One must also recite his name and keep that Buddha’s name in mind;
there is a Buddha in the western direction.
He is named Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vimalacandralakṣaṇarājaśrī;
you should likewise recite that Buddha’s name and cultivate respectful devotion toward him.
One must also recite his name and must also mentally keep that Buddha's name in mind.
In the northern direction there is a Buddha.
He is named Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Puṣpavyūhaprabhākara;
you should likewise recite that Buddha’s name and cultivate reverence toward him.
One must also recite his name and keep that Buddha’s name in mind.
In the southeast there is a Buddha.
His name is Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jyotirvidhāyaka.
You should likewise invoke that Buddha’s name and cultivate reverence toward him;
you must also recite his title.
One must also mentally recite the name of that Buddha:
In the southwestern direction,
there is a Buddha named Ratnottaralakṣaṇayaśas Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
One should likewise recite that Buddha’s name and practice respectful devotion;
one must also invoke his title and keep that Buddha’s name in mind.
In the northwest there is a Buddha named Abhayadṛśa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
One should likewise recite that Buddha’s name and cultivate reverence toward him.
One must also recite his name and must also keep that Buddha’s name in mind.
There is a Buddha in the northeast.
He is named Fearless and Undaunted, with Unbristling Body Hairs, Renowned Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
You should likewise invoke that Buddha’s name and cultivate reverence toward him.
One must also recite his name and keep that Buddha’s name in mind.
There is a Buddha in the lower direction.
He is named Siṃhavikrāntagāmin-Indriya Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha;
you should likewise invoke that Buddha’s name and cultivate reverence toward him.
One must also recite their name and keep that Buddha's name in mind.
There is a Buddha in the upper direction.
He is named Tathāgata Arhat Samyaksaṃbuddha King of Golden Light Majestic Majesty;
one should likewise recite that Buddha’s name and cultivate respectful devotion toward him.
One must also recite their name and must also mentally contemplate the name of that Buddha.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Maitreya.
If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family with right faith who,
while reciting the names of these twelve Buddhas,
practice repentance for all their transgressions for ten days, they shall [attain purification].
I rejoice in and entreat all sentient beings to cultivate every merit;
I beseech all Buddhas to remain long in the world.
With these roots of goodness, I dedicate them to the Dharma-realm.
At that time, one immediately attains the extinction of all transgressions and the purification of all karmic obstructions;
one immediately attains the full accomplishment of the adornment of all Buddha-fields.
They achieve and are fully endowed with fearlessness;
they further obtain a body fully adorned with the marks of excellence;
and they further obtain a retinue of bodhisattvas who surround them in full abundance.
Furthermore, they attain the full perfection of immeasurable dhāraṇīs;
furthermore, they attain the full perfection of immeasurable samādhis;
furthermore, they attain the full perfection of the adornments of buddha-fields according to their wishes.
They shall also come to possess immeasurable spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) and swiftly achieve,
without increase or decrease, that which has been described above;
they shall practice for the sake of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi) even while moving within the midst of afflictions (kleśa).
One obtains the retribution of being upright and pleasing to behold,
as well as an abundance of wealth and treasures,
and is always born into families of great lineage and noble descent.
They will be endowed with a perfect physical form and will also obtain a harmonious retinue surrounding them.
At that time, the World-Honored One, reiterating this meaning, spoke in verse:
"If there are sons of good family, or daughters of good family..."
By upholding the names of these Buddhas, one shall be loved and respected by others throughout every birth and lifetime;
possessing great brilliance and power,
one will be honored among humans in the places where one is born, and shall eventually attain Buddhahood.
The Buddha again addressed Maitreya:
"If there are good sons or good daughters who should receive and uphold the names of these Buddhas,"
One must also recite this dhāraṇī mantra:

*Ṣaḍbuddhā tiṣṭhanti* (37). At that time, having spoken this mantra, the World-Honored One further spoke these verses:
"Those who receive and uphold this mantra shall encounter sixty billion [Buddhas]."
The Buddhas of the ten directions now constantly keep this person in mind;
in all places of rebirth, they shall always encounter spiritual friends.
Whatever the heart desires and aspires for, all shall be auspicious.
By reciting this dhāraṇī, one shall always be born before all Buddhas upon exquisite lotus flowers;
through miraculous birth, one does not undergo gestation,
maintaining right mindfulness and right conduct, and increasing wisdom and other virtues.
Upon hearing it once, one fully retains it; what has been heard is never forgotten.
Those who receive and uphold this mantra obtain such merit as this;
and for those who recite these names of the Buddhas, wherever they are born, [they shall attain...]
Far removed from all evil realms, one swiftly attains rebirth in a favorable place;
having attained the concentration of dhāraṇī, one dwells in the most wondrous and supreme state,
upholding [the teachings] without forgetfulness until reaching bodhi.
All this arises from the names of the Buddhas and their dhāraṇīs.
If a person were to give the seven treasures filling thousands of millions of billions of lands,
the merit and reward of one who upholds these names of the Buddhas would exceed that.
Practicing the conduct of enlightenment, always remembering past lives and remaining far removed from all hardships,
one immediately attains a state of mastery,
is constantly born in buddha-fields where a Buddha resides, encounters the Buddhas, and hears the true Dharma.
Having attained the mind of faithful practice, and having attained this mind of faith,
one constantly makes offerings to the Buddhas; having encountered the Buddhas and heard the Dharma,
the mind gives rise to great joy, and having seen the various Buddhas, [one attains further realization].
Holding exquisite implements of offering, they make offerings to all Buddhas;
those who uphold the names of the Buddhas shall abandon the sins of birth and death for thousands of millions of billions of kalpas and swiftly accomplish the path of Buddhahood.
If a person can, with a sincere heart, recite the names of the Buddhas for seven days,
they will attain the pure eye and be able to see immeasurable Buddhas;
by upholding these names of the Buddhas, one immediately obtains immeasurable merit.
In whatever place such a person is born, gods and humans will always show them respect.
If a person upholds the name of the Buddha, for thousands of millions of billions of kalpas,
they shall not be insulted or humiliated by others throughout all worlds.
His fame shall spread far and wide; if a person upholds the name of the Buddha,
throughout thousands of millions of billions of kalpas, devas and humans will constantly make offerings to him,
and none shall ever disparage him, as he swiftly attains the Way of Buddhahood.
If a person upholds the name of the Buddha, they will not give rise to a mind of cowardice;
possessing wisdom free from flattery or crookedness, they will always remain before all Buddhas.
If a person upholds the name of the Buddha, wherever that person is born, [they shall be thus].
Gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas,
kiṃnaras, asuras, garuḍas, mahoragas, humans,
and non-humans— these shall always make offerings to such a person.
If a person upholds the names of the Buddhas, in every lifetime where they are born,
they will always be born into wealthy and noble families; they will be fully endowed with the marks of a great man,
free from stinginess and envy, and courageous and fond of giving.
From all the pores of the body, various wondrous fragrances constantly issue forth;
from between the teeth in the mouth, moreover, billowing scents emerge—
the fragrance of celestial red sandalwood and all other varieties of incense.
Throughout ten million billion kalpas, his fragrance shall never cease;
in every place where he is born from lifetime to lifetime, his voice shall be like that of Brahmā,
and like that of the kalaviṅka, the jīvajīvaka, and other such birds.
The merit of one who upholds the name of the Dharma King is likewise so.
If a person upholds the name of the Buddha, they shall be born amidst flowers of the seven precious gems;
those flowers possess a thousand billion petals, and they are fully endowed with majestic radiance and the marks of excellence.
If a person upholds the name of the Buddha, their parents and all kinsmen will have serene countenances and no disputes; they shall never experience separation.
Furthermore, if there are women who receive and uphold this sutra, [they shall likewise attain these benefits].
Having cast off the female form, one is reborn with the body of a wise man;
having attained the male body, one immediately realizes enlightenment and turns the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma,
entering nirvāṇa according to one’s will.
If a person upholds the name of the Buddha, blades and staves cannot harm them;
fire and water shall not burn or sweep them away; and officials shall not be able to kill them.
If a person upholds the name of the Buddha, neither the various māras nor Pāpīyān can prevail.
Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, no one can find an opportunity to harm them.
If a person upholds the name of the Buddha, in every life where they are born,
their body will have the supernormal power to travel through space and reach boundless lands.
Beholding the various Buddhas face-to-face, they are able to inquire about the most profound meanings;
those immeasurable Buddhas, knowing their mental dispositions,
preach the subtle and wondrous Dharma for them and bestow upon them the prediction of enlightenment.
Having heard the prophecy, their hearts were filled with great joy;
they became certain and free from doubt regarding the teachings of all Buddhas—
the profound Dharma spoken by those Blessed Ones, the World-Honored Ones.
Having heard the Dharma, that person receives and maintains it without ever losing it;
subsequently they shall achieve the six perfections, the various stages,
the fearlessnesses, the powers, and the primary and secondary marks of excellence.
Buddha-fields and sentient beings— taking whichever one pleases,
may they be born within those fields; swiftly attaining perfect enlightenment,
may they turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma, and according to their will, enter nirvana.
If there are good men and good women who receive and uphold this sutra,
they shall possess the merits as described above;
if one upholds this sutra, one should be prudent and not be negligent.
Hearing this merit from the aforementioned deeds— whether for the full duration of an eon or less than an eon—
one must always diligently recite it without giving rise to a mind of indolence; I have issued such an injunction.
These Buddhas dwell eternally within the treasury of merit, as kings amidst clouds in the sky; they abide forever in that place.
If a person hears the names of these Buddhas for even one kalpa, or less than a kalpa, [they shall attain liberation].
Having heard this, a heart of reverence arises:
he is the most heroic of men and possesses great wisdom;
he is the foremost among humanity and a true man of valor, renowned throughout the world.
Therefore, I now say: Maitreya, you should listen!
There are those of great wisdom who are skillful in means;
they are always diligent and never negligent, and they constantly draw near to virtuous friends.
Having heard this sutra, they shall subsequently proceed upon the path to Bodhi.
After the Buddha had spoken this sutra,
Maitreya Bodhisattva Mahāsattva...
As well as the assembly of bodhisattvas and the great assembly of bhikṣus;
and the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth.
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they rejoiced and practiced it accordingly.
This concludes the *Sūtra on the Recitation of the Divine Mantra of the Names of the Twelve Buddhas, the Measurement of Merit, and the Elimination of Obstacles and Destruction of Sins*.
